hotspots.title: Deceptive Root Domain & High-Risk TLD
hotspots.whatYouSee: The URL displays 'amazon' as part of a long hyphenated domain with an exotic '.xyz' extension.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: Attackers register cheap domains (like .xyz, .top, .buzz) with brand names hyphenated. Notice the connection uses unencrypted HTTP. The actual official root domain is amazon.in or amazon.com, never a hyphenated .xyz.
hotspots.defenseTip: Always inspect the root domain immediately preceding the TLD. If the domain contains hype words ('mega-loot', 'free-gift') or unusual extensions, navigate away immediately.

hotspots.title: Manufactured Panic & Fake Countdown Timer
hotspots.whatYouSee: An aggressive flashing red clock counting down seconds with fake notifications claiming other users just purchased.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: Cybercriminals exploit the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) cognitive bias. If you refresh the webpage, the timer resets back to 3 minutes. The urgency is engineered to prevent you from checking the URL or verifying the seller.
hotspots.defenseTip: Legitimate platforms do not give you 180 seconds before an authentic transaction is cancelled. Treat extreme artificial countdown clocks as an immediate scam signal.

hotspots.title: Absurd ₹99 Mega Deal Trap
hotspots.whatYouSee: A flagship luxury smartphone priced lower than a cup of coffee.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: This is a classic 'too good to be true' advance fee fraud. Even if you pay ₹99, no phone will ever ship. Furthermore, the payment page attempts to capture your UPI PIN or debit card CVV.
hotspots.defenseTip: If an offer defies economic reality, it is 100% fraud. Brand clearance sales never discount flagship luxury electronics by 99%.

hotspots.title: Unverified Personal UPI / Static QR Hijack
hotspots.whatYouSee: Direct prompt to scan a static personal QR code or transfer to an individual VPA instead of an authorized merchant gateway.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: Authorized e-commerce stores use RBI-compliant merchant gateways (Razorpay, BillDesk, Amazon Pay, PayU) that route through escrow. Direct personal VPAs offer zero consumer protection, cannot be refunded, and allow scammers to cash out immediately via mules.
hotspots.defenseTip: Never transfer money to a raw personal UPI VPA when shopping online. Legitimate checkouts trigger merchant payment requests with registered business names.

hotspots.title: Dead Footer Links & Bogus Compliance
hotspots.highlight: href='#' on all regulatory legal pages
hotspots.whatYouSee: Terms, Privacy Policy, and Contact Us links look clickable with official looking logos, but clicking them simply reloads the page or does nothing.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: Phishing kits copy the visual HTML/CSS snapshot of a homepage but strip or break auxiliary backend pages. Legitimate sites have detailed corporate terms, Grievance Officer details, and working refund policies.
hotspots.defenseTip: Before trusting an unknown shopping site, click on 'Privacy Policy' or 'Grievance Officer'. If the link goes to '#' or gives a 404, it is a scraped clone.

content.trapMechanism: Directly requests ATM PIN and SMS OTP on the initial login screen.

hotspots.title: Typosquatting with '.top' Extension
hotspots.whatYouSee: The domain begins with 'sbi-' followed by 'kyc-pan-update' ending in '.top'.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: Major Indian banks own their own gTLDs or official domains (e.g. .sbi, hdfcbank.com, icicibank.com). Attackers register domains ending in cheap extensions like '.top', '.club', or '.live'. Even though it shows 'https://' with a free Let's Encrypt lock, the owner is an individual scammer.
hotspots.defenseTip: A padlock icon only means communication is encrypted—it DOES NOT mean the website is legitimate. Verify the exact domain name letter-by-letter.

hotspots.title: Account Suspension Coercion
hotspots.whatYouSee: Bold red threat stating your bank account and debit card are already suspended or will freeze within 24 hours.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: Banks are legally required by the Reserve Bank of India to provide advance written notices and statutory grace periods before restricting accounts. Panic makes victims bypass their natural skepticism.
hotspots.defenseTip: Whenever you receive a threat of immediate bank account suspension, call your branch or official toll-free helpline directly. Never click the link in the message.

hotspots.title: Harvesting ATM PIN & Card Expiry
hotspots.highlight: Enter ATM PIN & CVV for KYC verification
hotspots.whatYouSee: The form asks for Debit Card Number, Expiry Date, CVV, and ATM PIN under the guise of 'Identity Verification'.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: No legitimate bank web form in the world ever asks for your 4-digit ATM PIN or card CVV to verify KYC. Once submitted, the attacker uses an automated API or POS terminal to drain your account balance immediately.
hotspots.defenseTip: Rule of thumb: Your ATM PIN is strictly for ATM machines and POS terminals. Never type your ATM PIN into any internet browser or webpage.

hotspots.title: Unregistered 10-Digit Mobile Sender
hotspots.highlight: Sent from +91-9876543210 instead of Header like 'VM-SBIINB'
hotspots.whatYouSee: Customer support contact is a personal 10-digit mobile number, or the SMS alert came from a personal SIM card.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: Under TRAI DLT regulations, official bank alerts MUST come from verified registered headers (e.g. AD-SBIINB, VK-HDFCBK, AX-ICICIB). Scammers use unregistered SIM cards or VoIP forwarding.
hotspots.defenseTip: If a banking notification comes from a standard 10-digit phone number (+91-9xxxx or +91-8xxxx), it is an illegal phishing attack.

hotspots.title: Non-Government Domain (.support vs .gov.in)
hotspots.whatYouSee: A domain with 'indiapost' in the string ending in '.support'.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: All legitimate central and state government portals in India strictly operate on '.gov.in' or '.nic.in' domains. Commercial and generic extensions (.support, .com, .site) are never used for official public postal services.
hotspots.defenseTip: Check the domain extension: If a supposed Indian Government website does not end with '.gov.in', do not interact with it.

hotspots.title: Dangerous APK Sideloading Trap
hotspots.whatYouSee: The website urges you to download an Android application file (.apk) directly from the browser instead of the Google Play Store.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: This is a banking trojan / SMS stealer. When installed, it asks for 'Accessibility' and 'SMS' permissions, allowing scammers in the background to read all your two-factor authentication codes and drain your accounts without your knowledge.
hotspots.defenseTip: NEVER install '.apk' files downloaded from websites or links received via SMS/WhatsApp. Only install applications through the official Google Play Store.

hotspots.title: Micro-Fee Gateway Credential Harvesting
hotspots.highlight: Pay nominal fee of ₹10 to re-route delivery
hotspots.whatYouSee: A tiny charge of ₹5 or ₹10 that seems negligible to most users.
hotspots.whyItsMalicious: The scammer doesn't care about the ₹10. The payment form is a phishing skimmer designed to capture your full 16-digit debit card number, CVV, and expiration date. Once you enter it, an international e-commerce transaction for ₹50,000+ is triggered.
hotspots.defenseTip: Postal and courier companies do not demand online micro-surcharges via SMS links for address corrections. Return/reschedule policies are handled at the doorstep.
